thread.title: NYS drivers will face harsher penalties for traffic violations - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: NYS drivers will face harsher penalties for traffic violations - NewsBreak

author: Jim Ehmke
title: NYS drivers will face harsher penalties for traffic violations - NewsBreak
text:
By Jim Ehmke ,
7 hours ago
BINGHAMTON, N.Y. (WIVT/WBGH) – The penalties for a long list of traffic infractions and vehicle crimes just got a lot heavier in New York State.
Broome County District Attorney Paul Battisti is warning motorists that the Department of Motor Vehicles has increased the number of points associated with certain offenses and added them to other crimes.
In particular, DWI and DWAI, also known as 1192, will now incur 11 points on a driver’s license in addition to fines and potential jail time.
Points also went up for aggravated unlicensed operation, passing a stopped school bus, speeding in a construction zone and leaving the scene of a personal injury accident.
Battisti says DWI charges already could lead to a judge suspending a driver’s license, although many could get conditional licenses to drive to and from work. He says the new rules put that in question, as the 11 points for DWI would be enough to trigger a suspension on its own.
“Is somebody eligible for a hardship license? Is somebody eligible for a conditional license? If they are eligible for a conditional license under the 1192, is that going to apply to the points system? A lot of these things, I don’t think we know yet. It’s going to be one of those things where the law’s been changed, there’s new points, we’ll see how the first case is handled and then we’ll go from there,” said Battisti,
The new system went into effect on Monday. It also increased the look-back period for accruing points from 18 months to two years.
Battisti says certain offenses, such as speeding, can still be resolved through the DA’s traffic diversion program. He says he is concerned that the harsher penalties may prompt more drivers facing misdemeanors to opt for a trial rather than a plea, increasing his office’s workload.
